transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-02-23
Start time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Ari (SilverCove), Priya (Platform Eng), Tom (CTO)
Notes/links: partner deck (drive.redwood/partner-spec.pdf), initial benchmark sheet (sheets.redwood/silvercove-bench)

Summary:
A first intro between Redwood AE/SE and SilverCove leadership to explore an edge-SaaS reseller/integration partnership. Topics: routing to hybrid infra, VPC/on-prem options, GPU capacity & margins, SSO/KMS/compliance needs, pilot sizing and benchmark plan. High-level interest from SilverCove in offering Redwood-hosted and a private (VPC) option to their customers through a managed integration.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for taking the time, really quick intros on our side. I'm Maya, I'm the account lead, and Jordan's our solutions engineer who will talk through the technical fit.
[00:18] Ari (SilverCove): thanks, Maya. Ari here, I run cloud partnerships at SilverCove. joining Priya and Tom. appreciate the time.
[00:26] Jordan (Redwood SE): hi all, Jordan — focus on serving/runtime and infra options. quick agenda we sent: integration patterns, security/compliance, pilot scope, commercial model. any changes?
[00:37] Tom (SilverCove): no that's good. we're looking at options to resell LLM inference to our edge customers — mix of hosted and VPC. latency is a big deal, and some customers are strict on residency.

[01:02] Priya (SilverCove): to add, many of our customers run on a lightweight edge agent + regional pools, so the ability to route to on-prem or regional GPU clusters is important. we also need to understand SSO and audit logs for our MSP offering.

[01:35] Maya: great, yes. at a high level Redwood supports three deployment modes: hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC/on-prem. we can expose those to partners via partner SKUs. quick Q: do you intend to run a managed offering where SilverCove owns the customer relationship and we operate the runtime, or do you want a reseller model where you host the runtime?
[01:58] Ari: primary is SilverCove-managed SaaS — we want to bundle inference as an add-on to our edge product. initially we want Redwood to host the models and runtime, then evaluate a private deployment option for regulated customers.

[02:20] Jordan: that maps well. common approach — start hosted for speed, then move to VPC or on-prem for customers with residency/AZ constraints. we do automatic fallback routing too so requests can go to a compatible variant if capacity is constrained.

[02:52] Tom: what does "compatible variant" mean? like lower precision quantized models?
[02:57] Jordan: yeah, exactly. we have quantized variants and model routing policies — we can fall back from, say, an fp16 model to an int8 quantized variant that is similar quality but lower cost. sometimes folks call it "graceful degradation."

[03:28] Priya: our edge customers will care about latency guarantees. can Redwood provide SLOs per route? and how do we instrument that?
[03:36] Jordan: yes — Redwood Console has per-route latency and token-level breakdowns. we push traces and metrics to your observability stack and also keep audit logs. for partner-managed customers we can enable extended retention for logs.

[04:12] Ari: security and compliance are huge. SOC 2 is required, many want SAML/SSO and KMS support for keys. also need assurance on data retention and auditability.
[04:24] Maya: all standard asks. Redwood is SOC 2 Type II (we will share cert). we support SAML SSO for the console and per-tenant RBAC. for keys we integrate with AWS KMS and customer HSMs in private deployments. audit logs are available and can be forwarded to your SIEM.

[05:00] Tom: good. for private deployments — what's the uplift on cost and support? some of our customers expect we host on their premises.
[05:09] Jordan: private deployments carry a platform fee and support contract; there's also the model of Dedicated reserved pools which is for you to reserve capacity in our infra. on-prem is a heavier lift — we have an on-prem package for air-gapped setups and we work with your infra team. we can outline typical T-shirt pricing ranges in the spec.

[05:45] Ari: pricing and margin are going to determine if this is viable for us — we need clear list vs reseller pricing. also curious about telemetry — will SilverCove see usage breakdown per end-customer?
[05:58] Maya: yes, our partner SKUs include per-customer metering and token attribution so you can invoice downstream. margins: we typically provide partner price tiers at commit levels. we'll include a sample partner rate card in the follow-up.

[06:28] Priya: operationally, how do you handle KV cache and prefix caching? some customers have long context windows and we'd like caching to reduce cost.
[06:36] Jordan: we do prefix/KV caching in the runtime; that's one of the main levers to reduce per-token cost. quick note: the system sometimes shows as "K-V cash" in transcriptions, but it's KV cache. we also provide suggestions on batching and quantization per workload via Redwood Optimize.

[07:12] Ari: model onboarding — how fast can we get a new model into the catalog? our customers sometimes want specialized models or tuned variants.
[07:20] Jordan: model onboarding depends on the model and compatibility with our optimized kernels. for common open models it's days; for custom, tuned variants it's a more involved onboarding and test cycle. we have a verification process with perf profiles.

[07:48] Speaker 1: (mumble) do we support region pinning...
[07:52] Maya: yes, region pinning and routing policies are supported — can pin by tenant or route and we can fallback across regions if permitted.

[08:18] Tom: on the host vs private tradeoff — many of our SMB customers want low latency but don't want the ops burden. Likely hosted for SMBs, private for enterprise customers. would the partner contract allow us to mix both for different customers?
[08:32] Maya: absolutely. the partner contract and SKUs are flexible — you can mix hosted for some customers and private/dedicated for others under the same reseller account.

[09:05] Priya: what about DLP/exfiltration controls? we have to be able to enforce data masking and restrict model outputs for some clients.
[09:14] Jordan: we offer plugin points for content filters and can enforce per-tenant output redaction rules, plus audit trails of requests/outputs. in private deployments you can also run local filters inside your network.

[09:47] Ari: Piloting — we'd want to run a pilot with 2-3 customers: one SMB on hosted, one regulated customer on VPC, and one high-throughput edge customer. looking for a 6–8 week pilot ideally.
[10:02] Maya: sounds reasonable. typical pilot components: 1) integration spec and authentication, 2) sample traffic for benchmarks, 3) success criteria (latency < Xms p95, cost target, accuracy on evaluation prompts), 4) timeline and rollouts.

[10:30] Tom: can we get a sample benchmark plan? we have some internal sims but we'd like Redwood to propose test harness and metrics.
[10:36] Jordan: yes — Jordan will draft a benchmark sheet (latency p50/p95, throughput qps, tokens/sec, cost per 1M tokens) and include steps for hosted and private runs.

[11:05] Priya: technical Q — our runtime uses a scaled edge agent that prefetches KV context. will Redwood's runtime accept pre-warmed KV cache tokens or do we need to rehydrate?
[11:17] Jordan: we can accept pre-warmed KV cache via our KV API. for private deployments it's straightforward; hosted has controlled cache interfaces for multi-tenant safety. we'll include exact API calls in the spec doc.

[11:45] Ari: integration timeline — how fast can we move to production for the hosted pilot?
[11:52] Maya: once contracts are signed, hosted pilot usually takes 2–3 weeks for basic integration, up to 6–8 for full evaluation and canarying. private/VPC pilot will add effort for networking and keys — add ~3–6 weeks depending on approvals.

[12:20] Tom: curious about model versions and rollouts — can we pin a customer to a specific model version and test canaries?
[12:27] Jordan: yes, you can pin model versions and run canary rollouts and A/B tests via Redwood Console. we also support automatic fallback policies.

[12:45] Speaker 2 (automated note): (brief noise)

[13:10] Ari: questions on margin mechanics — how are partner discounts structured? is there a minimum commit?
[13:18] Maya: we typically have tiered discounts depending on monthly commitments. no hard minimum for trial, but partner pricing improves with committed reserved capacity. we'll include example tiers in the pricing sheet.

[13:45] Priya: what about SLA for uptime and latency? we need a clear SLA for enterprise contracts.
[13:52] Jordan: dedicated and private contracts can include SLA commitments (uptime and latency targets) and escalation paths. hosted has standard SLAs which we can outline. for enterprise we also offer guaranteed throughput windows via reserved pools.

[14:25] Ari: data residency — if a customer requires EU-only data at rest and in transit, can the hosted option be limited to EU regions?
[14:34] Jordan: yes, region-specific hosting is supported and we can constrain data to EU regions. also VPC/private deployments can be located in EU if required.

[15:00] Tom: for the pilot, we'll need a list of required firewall ports and networking configuration.
[15:06] Jordan: will include a networking checklist (eg. ports for gRPC, NAT, peering details for VPC).

[15:34] Ari: around support model — we'd expect a partner-rolled support layer, but Redwood to provide SE hours during pilot. is that included?
[15:42] Maya: for pilots we include a limited allocation of SE hours; for long-term partnerships there's a partner success SLA. we'll propose a support cadence in the follow-up.

[16:05] Priya: any known integration gotchas with our stack? we run k3s clusters at regionals and an internal service mesh.
[16:13] Jordan: k3s is fine; main considerations are GPU drivers and compatible CUDA/cuDNN versions in private/on-prem. we'll share recommended images and kernel lists. also, quantized kernel support varies a bit by GPU generation.

[16:40] Tom: who would be our primary contact at Redwood for day-to-day?
[16:44] Maya: me for commercial and Jordan for technical. we'll also introduce an integration manager if we proceed.

[17:05] Ari: great. on commercial — would love the initial partner rate card and an example contract flow so we can review with legal.
[17:12] Maya: yeah we'll send a partner pack: rate card, sample contract terms, SOC2 cert, and deployment checklist.

[17:35] Priya: one last technical concern — can we run model explainability hooks or are model internals blocked for hosted customers?
[17:44] Jordan: we provide token-level traces and some internal metrics; deep model internals for closed models may be limited. for open models and private deployments you get more visibility. we'll call that out in the spec.

[18:10] (brief cross-talk)

Recap and next steps:
[18:20] Maya: quick recap — Redwood to send partner integration spec, sample rate card, SOC2 docs, benchmark proposal. SilverCove to share workload profile, top pilot customers, and networking constraints. schedule tech deep dive week of 2026-03-09.

[18:45] Ari: sounds good. target to review docs internally and pick pilot customers by end of next week.

[19:00] Tom: thanks everyone, excited to run a pilot.

[19:06] Maya: thanks all, will follow up with the pack and calendar invites.

(End of recording)
